text:
InfraBot: :rotating_light: Pager -> oncall Maya: Elevated 5xx and connection timeouts observed from private inference-gateway (igw-private-*-us-west-2). Alert: gateway-5xx-spike-286543 -> start 12:34 UTC. Affected: customer-dedicated clusters (subset).
Maya: Acked. I'm on it. Linking runbook: <https://redwood-internal/runbooks/egress-nat-5xx>.
Sam: FYI I just pushed a security-group tightening to the transit-peers stack ~12:20 UTC (restricting ephemeral range to 49152-65535). Could be related.
Maya: Noted. Initial graphs show 5xx surge correlating with increased TCP RST to upstreams and a rise in SNAT errors on the nat-appliance.
Maya: Quick checks: `ss -tnp state TIME-WAIT` shows a lot of RSTs; `dmesg` has `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet`.
Sam: Oof. conntrack saturation makes sense if ephemeral range narrowed and connections churn. Sample conntrack dump (sanitized):
```
# conntrack -L | head
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.8.12 dst=52.45.123.9 sport=45012 dport=443 packets=128 bytes=10324 [ASSURED]
tcp      6 29 TIME_WAIT src=10.0.8.13 dst=52.45.67.3 sport=52000 dport=443 packets=4 bytes=312
nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
Maya: That `table full` line matches our alerts. Also seeing `504 gateway timeout` in gateway logs with `connect to upstream failed: connection reset by peer`.
Jordan: I'm jumping in for networking. If conntrack is full, new flows get dropped -> TLS handshakes fail -> clients see 5xx/timeouts. Likely interplay of SG ephemeral windows + churn from recent canary traffic.
Maya: Can we confirm if SG change reduced ephemeral range? Sam?
Sam: Yes, applied patch narrowed allowed egress ports to 49152-65535 on the peering SG. Previously we allowed 32768-65535. Some customers' SDKs open high-numbered ephemeral ports near 32000.
Maya: That would explain packets hitting peering and being RST/blocked. Two parallel things: (1) conntrack max too low for current flows, (2) SG mismatch causing retransmits and resets.
Maya: Mitigation plan (short):
- open temporary rollback on peering SG to 32768-65535
- raise conntrack max on nat-appliances to 524288 via sysctl and reload conntrack tunables
- add temporary iptables MASQUERADE rule on standby transit appliance to offload SNAT while we stabilize
- failover BGP to secondary transit path for a subset of gateways if errors persist
Sam: I'll revert the SG rule now to 32768-65535 for the transit-peers security group and push as hotfix. ETA 2m.
Sam: (push done) Reverted SG range, applied to all transit-peers in us-west-2.
Maya: Confirming packet acceptance on the peering interface with `tcpdump`: seeing SYN->SYN/ACK completed on previously failing flows.
Maya: Increasing conntrack: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` on nat-appliance-1 and -2, then `echo 524288 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`.
Jordan: Also bumped `conntrack_hashsize` and tuned `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` lower for churny workloads. Commands run:
```
echo 131072 > /sys/module/nf_conntrack/parameters/hashsize
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```
Maya: Temp MASQUERADE on transit-standby to take some SNAT load: `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth1 -j MASQUERADE` on transit-standby-3. Added with comment `temp offload 5xx-286543`.
Maya: Observing error rate drop in the last 3m: 5xx from 18% -> 2.5%. Latency returning to baseline. :white_check_mark:
Maya: Customer impact: Affected ~6 dedicated clusters; heavy success rate reduction for customer-alpha and customer-gamma during window 12:34-12:40 UTC. We sent an incident banner to customers via status page and CS.
Ops-Lead: Good work. Please prepare a short blameless summary for postmortem with timings, root cause hypothesis (SG ephemeral range + conntrack saturation + churn), mitigations applied, and follow-ups.
Jordan: Taking over on-call for next hour to watch for recurrence and coordinate followups. Handoff notes:
- SG revert remains in place (we'll plan a staged, tested rollout of tighter range)
- conntrack max raised; consider permanent increase or autoscaling nat-appliances
- add monitoring alert for `nf_conntrack: table full` and ephemeral port utilization per transit
- run customer traffic replay against staging with tightened SG to reproduce
Maya: Adding follow-ups to infra backlog: ticket INFRA-8421 (permanent conntrack tuning + runbook update), INFRA-8422 (SG rollout validation + canary tests), INFRA-8423 (BGP failover playbook).
Maya: Anything else before I hand to Jordan?
Sam: I'll add a note: avoid tightening ephemeral range below 32768 across peering without compatibility test.
Jordan: I'll keep monitoring. If I see a spike, I'll fail traffic to the alternate peering and escalate.
Ops-Lead: Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated and starting a P0 -> P1 de-escalation. Please attach logs and commands you ran to INFRA-8421.
Maya: Uploading logs + tcpdumps to the incident folder now. End of live thread.
